lead: it was finished at noon and in the shop by two, because finished is when you show things. four people had the measurements off it before you went home, without anybody having to ask.
sun: what comes off your bench is good enough that the trade names it by your name, and it goes out exactly as it left your hands — no terms on it, nothing withheld to sell later, nothing sanded off the front so the method stays yours longer. the admiration and the copying are one event. the man praising the joint is reading how it was cut while he says it.
moon: a finished thing goes onto the bench in front of whoever is in the shop, weeks before it is ready to sell and years before it is worth money. the nine that came to nothing went up the same way, in the same daylight, and got looked at as closely. so the trade holds your failures too, each one with your name said over it.
pull: your name is on the method and the method is in six other shops. nobody stole anything. they were standing there when you finished it, because you called them in.
tension: generous is what it gets called to your face. the word used when you are out of the room is soft, and both get said about the same afternoon. younger men have made steadier livings off what you demonstrated than you have made doing it, and they say so, with credit, in public, at trade suppers, which leaves you nothing to be aggrieved about. no complaint you could raise would survive being spoken aloud.
cost: a thing that works reaches the room the week it works, and everybody within reach of your bench is a decade ahead of the trade elsewhere. the work arrives uncovered, in front of witnesses, and by the season you might have thought about terms, six shops are running it and telling customers whose it is. being credited and being paid turn out to be separate arrangements.

lead: every visitor for eleven years has been walked down that hall and told who made it. the family's best argument is an object, and you made it at twenty-four, and your mother has the story exactly right.
sun: what you made is good, and it is in their keeping now, doing a job you did not assign it. the house uses it to explain itself: whatever went on in there, look what came out. you handed it over the way you hand everything over, finished, with no conditions on it and no sentence attached about what it was made out of. it works better as their evidence than it ever worked as yours.
moon: the account that would correct the hall has run the full length of you since you were fifteen and has never been out. the day is yours to name and you have named it not yet, every year, and that gets easier because the object on the wall is doing the talking. what would have been a hard evening at thirty is a demolition now.
pull: they show your work to visitors as proof of what that house was. you built the exhibit for a case you would testify against, and it is signed.
tension: at gatherings you are the good outcome, and their warmth about it is real, which is what makes it immovable. any account you gave now would open by taking down a thing they love, made by you, in front of cousins who were children in that house and remember a different one. nobody at that table is lying. they are quoting an object, and the object is beautiful, and you made it beautiful on purpose.
cost: you can put a thing into the world that reads correctly to a stranger in four seconds, and your family read it the same way and took it home, where it is now load-bearing. what you carry stays at full term behind it. every year the hall does its work the sentence gets dearer, until saying it would cost more than the thing was ever worth to you.

lead: a client tells you what people charge for this and quotes back a figure you have never said aloud. seven of you in the city make that figure true, and yours is the piece in the photograph.
sun: being visibly the best of the seven puts no floor under anything. the work goes out finished and looked at with your name on it, and the number travelling beside it was arrived at somewhere else, by people who liked it. the sentence that holds a price — this is what mine costs, and here is why — has never been in your mouth, and nobody has noticed it is missing.
moon: from the hiring side the seven of you are one line item with a rate on it, and up close it separates: two who cannot do what you do, one who taught you, four somewhere between. an afternoon of looking properly would settle it. a single rate makes the looking unnecessary, so you have been quoted your own group's average, warmly, every year for a decade.
pull: you are the reason people pay the rate. you are paid the rate. to everyone who has ever paid it, the seven of you are one number with seven faces.
tension: raising it makes you the one who broke the number, and the six are your friends — they pass you work, you have slept on their floors. the argument would have to be made against the people who made it unnecessary. and in the thin year the rate held and the seven went to four, which sorted nobody by quality: the ones who left had rent due, and the ones who stayed had somebody else earning.
cost: strangers who know nothing about the trade pick your piece out of a line of seven on the way past, every time, and the picking-out is where it stops. the figure comes in from outside, settled by six other people and every client who has ever asked one of them, and a decade of being singled out by eye has not moved it by a note in any direction.

lead: you go in behind him and you come out behind him, and you have been able to leave him since the second decade. the body that came of it is the first thing anybody mentions about you.
sun: a body is a made thing here, and yours shows its making: what you eat and at which hour and for how many years is legible on you to anybody across a table. it gets remarked on out loud, in company, by doctors and in-laws and strangers at the pool, and the flat sentence that ends a subject was never issued to you. you stand there and take the appraisal like weather.
moon: his pace is the ceiling and you have held a length under it every morning for twenty years, chosen each time, said to nobody. the plate goes the same way — you stop where he stops. so what people admire is the accumulation of a limit set behind another man's shoulder, held at that setting through two of his injuries and one of yours.
pull: you have been the stronger of the two for twenty years, a length back, on purpose. everybody who compliments your body is describing a ceiling you chose and never mentioned to anyone.
tension: what you refuse at a table gets read as vanity, because the evidence is sitting right there making the case, and a man built like that declining the second plate looks like a man minding an investment. hunger is the true word for it and it would not be believed. so the compliments keep coming, weekly, from people who mean every one of them, each asking you to agree that this was what it was for.
cost: twenty years of a hard line has cost you nothing you have noticed — the hour, the plate, the cold water, steady where other people's discipline arrives and departs. all of it ended up on the outside of you where anyone can reach it and comment, and no move of yours closes that conversation. the year it starts to go, the same people will see it first.
